_comment: On-demand deep audit — deliberately NOT a gate and NOT in CI.
Measured on this repo:
src/lib/date-utils.ts    2 mutants, dependent suite   57 tests / net 0.08s -> 4s      score 100.00
src/lib/task-markers.ts 57 mutants, dependent suite  416 tests / net 54.2s -> 9m09s   score  89.47 (6 survived, 11 timeout)
Cost is the PRODUCT of two things, and neither alone predicts it:
(1) how many mutants are STATIC — Stryker reports 26 of 57 here (46%) and
warns they take ~100% of the runtime. A static mutant sits in
module-level code (this module's two regex constants), so the module
must be reloaded and coverageAnalysis:perTest cannot narrow it.
(2) how big the module's DEPENDENT SUITE is — what one un-narrowed run
costs. 416 tests / 54.2s here against 57 tests / 0.08s for date-utils.
26 x 54.2s at concurrency 4 accounts for the bulk of the 549s. Measured
directly: `--ignoreStatic` takes the same run to 63.8s — 8.6x faster.
That flag is a real lever with a real cost, not a free win: those 26 mutants
then go untested and are reported as survived, so the score falls 89.47 ->
45.61. Reach for it to iterate, not to report a number.
The 11 timeouts are NOT margin. Stryker's ceiling is timeoutFactor(1.5) x
netTime + timeoutMS + overhead, and a static mutant's netTime is the whole
un-narrowed suite — so the ceiling here is ~144s while a normal static run
is ~54s, well under it. All 11 are Regex mutants on the two module-level
constants, and every one WIDENS what the pattern accepts (anchor dropped,
\s+ -> \s, {0,3} -> {}): parseTaskLine then accepts lines it should
reject and the real-fixture consumers do enough extra work to blow past
144s. Timeouts also score as KILLED, so a loaded machine reports a HIGHER
score — never compare scores across machines.
Budget by (module-level constants?) x (how much of the suite reaches it?).
A module with only one of the two is cheap. A gate at minutes-per-module
gets switched off rather than satisfied.
NOT a usable metric: `tests per mutant` is bistable on this repo — the same
date-utils command returned 5.00 and 1.00 across byte-identical runs. It is
deliberately absent from the figures above.
Surviving mutants are a signal to read, not a defect list — equivalence is a
human judgment the tool cannot make.
plugins MUST be declared: pnpm's strict node_modules layout stops Stryker
from discovering the runner on its own.
mutate defaults to the module measured above so a bare `npx stryker run
stryker.config.json` reproduces that figure instead of walking all of
src/lib (35 files) unbounded. `pnpm mutate <path>` requires an explicit path.
